subproblems.title: Coordinate expansion of covectors in the basis dx^β
subproblems.statement:
For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n:
α = Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β,
where I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P is the finite type of order embeddings β : Fin n ↪o Fin P, α(e_β) = euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β = α(e_{β(0)},…,e_{β(n−1)}) with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, and dx^β = wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n), α = ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β • wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent proof with Q = identity ("With Q = identity, the same sibling gives φ = Σ_{β∈I} φ(e_β)·dx^β"). The parent takes this from its dependency covector_rotated_expansion (a dependency of the parent node, not of this child), whose own proof establishes exactly this standard expansion (its Steps 1–2) before rotating. This child has no dependencies, so those steps are reproduced here, with the details of the accepted proof of the identical comparator-accepted declaration cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge (DAG node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.covector_expansion-a1, candidate 6c6b4b2753e8214a3e45619bb0b65d8d553557a5).
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). For a tuple v : Fin n → Fin P, e_v := (e_{v(0)}, …, e_{v(n−1)}). For β ∈ I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P, α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β and dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. Kronecker property. Let β, γ ∈ I(n,P). By wedgeCovectors_apply_det, dx^β(e_γ) = det M, where M_{ij} = proj(β(i))(e_{γ(j)}) is 1 if β(i) = γ(j) and 0 otherwise.
 (a) If β = γ, then M_{ij} = 1 iff β(i) = β(j) iff i = j, because β is injective. So M is the identity matrix and dx^β(e_β) = 1.
 (b) If β ≠ γ, some i has β(i) ∉ {γ(0), …, γ(n−1)}. Otherwise range β ⊆ range γ; both ranges have exactly n elements because β and γ are injective (Set.ncard_range_of_injective), so range β = range γ (Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le); an order embedding of the well-order Fin n is determined by its range (OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so β = γ, a contradiction. For this i, row i of M is zero, hence det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero).
 Thus dx^β(e_γ) = δ_{βγ}.
2. Agreement on increasing tuples. Let R := Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} α(e_β)·dx^β, a continuous alternating n-linear map. For γ ∈ I(n,P), Step 1 gives R(e_γ) = Σ_β α(e_β)·δ_{βγ} = α(e_γ).
3. Agreement on injective tuples. Let v : Fin n → Fin P be injective, and let σ := Tuple.sort v, a permutation of Fin n with v∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). Since v∘σ is also injective, it is strictly increasing, so γ := v∘σ defines an element of I(n,P) (OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono) with e_γ = e_v∘σ. For every alternating map f, f(e_v∘σ) = sign(σ)·f(e_v) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). Applying this to α and to R and using Step 2 gives sign(σ)·α(e_v) = α(e_γ) = R(e_γ) = sign(σ)·R(e_v). Acting with sign(σ)⁻¹ (inv_smul_smul) yields α(e_v) = R(e_v).
4. Agreement on all basis tuples. If v : Fin n → Fin P is not injective, e_v has two equal entries, so α(e_v) = 0 = R(e_v) because both maps are alternating.
5. Conclusion. Two alternating multilinear maps on ℝ^P that agree on all tuples (e_{v(0)}, …, e_{v(n−1)}) with v injective are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating, applied to the basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis; Step 4 shows that the non-injective tuples agree as well). Hence α and R are equal as alternating maps, and therefore as continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). So α = Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β.
6. Degenerate cases are covered by Steps 1–5. For n = 0, I(0,P) has exactly one element, dx^β is the constant covector 1, and the identity reads α = α(())·1. For n > P, I(n,P) is empty, so R = 0, and no injective v exists, so Step 5 gives α = 0 = R. ∎
proof_key_steps: Kronecker property: dx^β(e_γ) = det[δ_{β(i)γ(j)}] = δ_{βγ} for β, γ ∈ I(n,P).
R := Σ_β α(e_β)·dx^β agrees with α on every increasing basis tuple e_γ.
Sorting an injective index tuple (Tuple.sort, AlternatingMap.map_perm) gives agreement on all injective basis tuples; non-injective tuples give 0 on both sides.
Module.Basis.ext_alternating and injectivity of toAlternatingMap give α = R.

subproblems.title: A covector coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every n-covector α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n and every strictly increasing multi-index β ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P): |α(e_β)| ≤ |α|. Here α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β = α(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}) with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing]·α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})²) with b_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n) (β : SimonMultiIndex n P), |euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof ("For every n-covector φ and β ∈ I, |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ|. Indeed, the strictly increasing map β is one of the indices of the sum |φ|² = Σ_{J strictly increasing} φ(e_J)², and all terms are ≥ 0"), with the details of the accepted proof of the identical comparator-accepted declaration cmb_rb_abs_euclideanCovectorCoordinate_le (DAG node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.repr_bound-a1.coord_bound-a1, candidate bc4ced0777075cca0b2e8f7beba5ba914fae595c).

1. By definition covectorEuclideanNorm α = √S with S := Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} a_I, where a_I := α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})² if I is strictly increasing and a_I := 0 otherwise, and b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. Every a_I is ≥ 0, being a square or 0.
2. For every i, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
3. Put I₀ := (j ↦ β j) : Fin n → Fin P. Since β is an order embedding, I₀ is strictly increasing (OrderEmbedding.strictMono). By Steps 1–2, a_{I₀} = α(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)})² = t², where t := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β = α(fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (β j) 1) by definition.
4. All summands of S are nonnegative, so one summand is at most the sum: t² = a_{I₀} ≤ S (Finset.single_le_sum over Finset.univ).
5. Hence |t| = √(t²) ≤ √S = covectorEuclideanNorm α, by Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs and the monotonicity of √ (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt). ∎
Edge cases: for n = 0 the unique empty tuple is strictly increasing and the argument is unchanged. If n > P, then SimonMultiIndex n P is empty and the statement is vacuous.
proof_key_steps: |α|² = S is a sum of nonnegative terms a_I over all I : Fin n → Fin P.
I₀ := (j ↦ β j) is strictly increasing and basisFun i = single i 1, so a_{I₀} = α(e_β)².
One nonnegative summand is ≤ the sum, so |α(e_β)| = √(α(e_β)²) ≤ √S = |α|.

subproblems.title: Evaluation bound for a covector at any tuple: |φ(v)| ≤ (Σ_β |dx^β(v)|)·|φ| (Step 4(a) of the parent proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let φ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n be an n-covector on ℝ^P and let v : Fin n → Eucl P be an n-tuple of vectors of ℝ^P. Then |φ(v)| ≤ (Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} |dx^β(v)|)·|φ|. Here I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P is the finite type of order embeddings Fin n ↪o Fin P, dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)), and |φ| := covectorEuclideanNorm φ is Simon's Euclidean coefficient norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (φ : Covector (Eucl P) n) (v : Fin n → Eucl P), |φ v| ≤ (∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, |wedgeCovectors n (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.proj (β j) : Eucl P →L[ℝ] ℝ)) v|) * covectorEuclideanNorm φ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4(a) of the parent proof ("If |φ| ≤ 1 then |φ(e^Q_α)| ≤ c_α. By Step 2 with Q = id, φ(e^Q_α) = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β(e^Q_α), and |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ| ≤ 1 by Step 3"), with the tuple e^Q_α replaced by an arbitrary tuple v and the bound 1 replaced by |φ|. The parent uses it with v := e^Q_α = (Q^{−1}e_{α(0)}, …, Q^{−1}e_{α(m)}) and |ω(x)| ≤ 1, which gives |ω(x)(e^Q_α)| ≤ c_α·|ω(x)| ≤ c_α with c_α = Σ_β |dx^β(e^Q_α)|.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, φ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate φ β = φ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}), dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)), |φ| := covectorEuclideanNorm φ.

1. Expansion. By the child theorem std_expansion (cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge, a dependency of this child) applied to φ, φ = Σ_{β∈I(n,P)} φ(e_β)·dx^β as continuous alternating maps. This is Step 2 of the parent proof with Q = id.
2. Evaluation at v. Evaluation at the fixed tuple v commutes with finite sums and scalar multiples of continuous alternating maps: (Σ_β f_β)(v) = Σ_β f_β(v) and (t·f)(v) = t·f(v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply). Evaluating the identity of Step 1 at v (rewrite only the left-hand occurrence of φ) gives φ(v) = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β(v).
3. Triangle inequality. |φ(v)| ≤ Σ_β |φ(e_β)·dx^β(v)| = Σ_β |φ(e_β)|·|dx^β(v)| (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, abs_mul).
4. Coordinate bound. By the child theorem coord_bound (cmb_rb_abs_euclideanCovectorCoordinate_le, a dependency of this child), |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ| for every β ∈ I(n,P); this is Step 3 of the parent proof. Since |dx^β(v)| ≥ 0, each term satisfies |φ(e_β)|·|dx^β(v)| ≤ |φ|·|dx^β(v)|.
5. Summation. Summing Step 4 over β and combining with Step 3: |φ(v)| ≤ Σ_β |φ|·|dx^β(v)| = |φ|·Σ_β |dx^β(v)| = (Σ_β |dx^β(v)|)·|φ| (Finset.mul_sum, commutativity of multiplication). ∎
If I(n,P) = ∅ (n > P), Step 1 gives φ = 0, both sides are 0, and the steps above apply verbatim.
proof_key_steps: Expand φ = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β (std_expansion) and evaluate at v: φ(v) = Σ_β φ(e_β)·dx^β(v).
Triangle inequality: |φ(v)| ≤ Σ_β |φ(e_β)|·|dx^β(v)|.
coord_bound gives |φ(e_β)| ≤ |φ| for each β; factor |φ| out of the sum.

subproblems.title: Pairing bound for a normalized n-vector: Σ_β w(dx^β)² = 1 implies |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)| (Step 4(b) of the parent proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let w ∈ NVector (Eucl P) n be an n-vector on ℝ^P (a continuous linear functional on Covector (Eucl P) n) and let θ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n be an n-covector. Assume Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} w(dx^β)² = 1, where I(n,P) = SimonMultiIndex n P, dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)) and w(dx^β) = euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β. Then |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_{β ∈ I(n,P)} |θ(e_β)|, where θ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β = θ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}) and e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n) (θ : Covector (Eucl P) n), ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, (euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β) ^ 2 = 1 → |w θ| ≤ ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, |euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β|
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4(b) of the parent proof ("By Step 2 with Q = id, θ_α = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·dx^β, so ξ(x)(θ_α) = Σ_β θ_α(e_β)·ξ(x)(dx^β) by linearity of ξ(x). At every x with Σ_β ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1 ... each |ξ(x)(dx^β)| ≤ 1, so |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α"), stated at a single point. The parent applies it with w := ξ(x) and θ := θ_α at every x where Σ_β ξ(x)(dx^β)² = 1, which holds for μ-a.e. x; this gives |ξ(x)(θ_α)| ≤ c'_α = Σ_β |θ_α(e_β)| for μ-a.e. x.
Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, θ(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate θ β = θ(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}), dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).

1. Unit coordinates. By definition, euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β = w(dx^β). Fix β ∈ I(n,P). All summands of Σ_γ w(dx^γ)² are squares, hence ≥ 0, so w(dx^β)² ≤ Σ_γ w(dx^γ)² = 1 (Finset.single_le_sum over Finset.univ). Hence |w(dx^β)| ≤ 1, because for real t, t² ≤ 1 iff |t| ≤ 1 (sq_le_one_iff_abs_le_one).
2. Expansion. By the child theorem std_expansion (cmb_covector_eq_sum_coord_smul_wedge, a dependency of this child) applied to θ, θ = Σ_β θ(e_β)·dx^β. This is Step 2 of the parent proof with Q = id.
3. Linearity. w is a linear map on covectors, so applying it to Step 2 (rewrite only the occurrence of θ inside w(θ)) gives w(θ) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·w(dx^β) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·euclideanNVectorCoordinate w β (map_sum, map_smul).
4. Estimate. By the triangle inequality and Step 1, |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|·|w(dx^β)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|·1 = Σ_β |θ(e_β)|, using |θ(e_β)| ≥ 0 (Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, abs_mul, mul_le_of_le_one_right). ∎
If I(n,P) = ∅, the hypothesis reads 0 = 1 and the statement holds vacuously.
proof_key_steps: Each |w(dx^β)| ≤ 1, since w(dx^β)² is one nonnegative summand of a sum equal to 1.
Expand θ = Σ_β θ(e_β)·dx^β (std_expansion) and apply the linear map w: w(θ) = Σ_β θ(e_β)·w(dx^β).
Triangle inequality: |w(θ)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|·|w(dx^β)| ≤ Σ_β |θ(e_β)|.

subproblems.title: A smooth compactly supported function times a constant covector is a test form in Dⁿ(U) (test-form claims of Steps 6–7 of the parent proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f, i.e. smooth of every finite order) with compact support (HasCompactSupport f) and tsupport f ⊆ U, and let θ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n be a fixed n-covector. Then there is a test form φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) (φ : TestFormOn U n) with φ(x) = f(x)·θ for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (θ : Covector (Eucl P) n), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ U → ∃ φ : TestFormOn U n, ∀ x, (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = f x • θ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the test-form claims of the parent proof, namely Step 6 ("The form ζ_α(x) := ω_α(x)·θ_α is a test form in Dⁿ(U)") and Step 7 ("φ₁ is C^∞ with tsupport φ₁ ⊆ tsupport ω_α ⊆ W ⊆ U"). Both are instances: f := ω_α, respectively f := ω_α·(b∘π_α), and θ := θ_α.
Recall that TestFormOn U n is the real submodule testFormOnSubmodule U n of DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n = (Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n). Its members ψ satisfy IsTestForm ψ, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ (∞ = ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) and HasCompactSupport ψ, and also tsupport ψ ⊆ U.

1. Candidate. Define ψ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n by ψ(x) := f(x)·θ.
2. Smoothness. ψ is the pointwise scalar product of the C^∞ function f and the constant, hence C^∞, map x ↦ θ. Scalar multiplication ℝ × Covector (Eucl P) n → Covector (Eucl P) n is continuous bilinear, so ψ is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul with contDiff_const).
3. Support. If f(x) = 0 then ψ(x) = 0. So support ψ ⊆ support f and tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport f (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
4. Compact support. tsupport ψ is a closed subset of the compact set tsupport f, hence compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport ψ (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
5. Domain. By Step 3 and the hypothesis, tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ U.
6. Conclusion. By Steps 2, 4 and 5, ψ ∈ testFormOnSubmodule U n. Let φ ∈ TestFormOn U n be ψ together with this membership proof. Then (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)(x) = ψ(x) = f(x)·θ for every x, by definition. ∎
proof_key_steps: ψ(x) := f(x)·θ is C^∞ as the scalar product of a C^∞ function and a constant map.
support ψ ⊆ support f, so tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ U and ψ has compact support.
Hence ψ lies in the submodule TestFormOn U n, and it has the required values.

subproblems.title: Representation estimate for a test form h·θ whose coefficient vanishes off W and on K: |T(hθ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K) (Step 7(b) of the parent proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, W, K ⊆ ℝ^P with W open and K compact. Let T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), let μ be a measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (NVector (Eucl P) n) with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ: for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x). Assume μ(W∖K) ≠ ∞. Let θ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n, h : ℝ^P → ℝ and c, c' ∈ ℝ satisfy: |h(x)| ≤ c for every x; h(x) = 0 for every x ∉ W; h(x) = 0 for every x ∈ K; and |ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c' for μ-a.e. x. Then every φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ(x) = h(x)·θ for all x satisfies |T(φ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K), where μ(W∖K) is read as a real number (ENNReal.toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W K : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ → IsOpen W → IsCompact K → μ (W \ K) ≠ ∞ → ∀ (θ : Covector (Eucl P) n) (h : Eucl P → ℝ) (c c' : ℝ), (∀ x, |h x| ≤ c) → (∀ x, x ∉ W → h x = 0) → (∀ x ∈ K, h x = 0) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |ξ x θ| ≤ c') → ∀ φ : TestFormOn U n, (∀ x, (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x = h x • θ) → |T φ| ≤ c * c' * (μ (W \ K)).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7(b) of the parent proof ("By the representation, T(φ₂) = ∫ g dμ with g(x) := ξ(x)(φ₂(x)) = ω_α(x)(1 − b(π_αx))·ξ(x)(θ_α), and g is μ-integrable. For μ-a.e. x, |g(x)| ≤ c_α c'_α·1_{W∖K}(x) ... Hence |T(φ₂)| ≤ ∫|g| dμ ≤ c_α c'_α·μ(W∖K)"), stated for a general coefficient h. The parent applies it with h := ω_α·(1 − b∘π_α), θ := θ_α, c := c_α, c' := c'_α and φ := φ₂.
Write A := W∖K and D := μ(A).toReal ≥ 0; here μ(A) ≠ ∞.

1. Integral formula. By IsMeasureRepresentation applied to φ, the function g(x) := ξ(x)(φ(x)) is μ-integrable and T(φ) = ∫ g dμ. Since ξ(x) is linear, g(x) = ξ(x)(h(x)·θ) = h(x)·ξ(x)(θ) for every x (map_smul).
2. Sign of c. The space ℝ^P contains 0, so c ≥ |h(0)| ≥ 0.
3. Dominating function. W is open and K is compact, hence closed, so both are Borel and A = W∖K is measurable (IsOpen.measurableSet, IsCompact.isClosed, IsClosed.measurableSet, MeasurableSet.diff). Let G := A.indicator (fun _ => c·c'). Since A is measurable and μ(A) ≠ ∞, G is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const), and ∫ G dμ = μ(A).toReal·(c·c') = c·c'·D (integral_indicator_const).
4. Pointwise domination. Let x satisfy |ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c'; by hypothesis this holds for μ-a.e. x.
 – If x ∈ A, then |g(x)| = |h(x)|·|ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c·|ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c·c' = G(x). The first inequality uses |ξ(x)(θ)| ≥ 0, the second uses c ≥ 0 (Step 2).
 – If x ∉ A, then x ∉ W or x ∈ K. In the first case h(x) = 0 by the hypothesis off W; in the second, h(x) = 0 by the hypothesis on K. Either way g(x) = 0 = G(x).
 Hence |g(x)| ≤ G(x) for μ-a.e. x.
5. Conclusion. By Steps 1, 3 and 4, |T(φ)| = |∫ g dμ| ≤ ∫ G dμ = c·c'·D (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). ∎
No sign assumption on c' is needed: if c' < 0, the a.e. hypothesis makes μ the zero measure and Steps 1–5 apply verbatim.
proof_key_steps: T(φ) = ∫ h(x)·ξ(x)(θ) dμ(x) by the representation and linearity of ξ(x).
c ≥ |h(0)| ≥ 0; A := W∖K is measurable with μ(A) ≠ ∞, so c·c'·1_A is integrable with integral c·c'·μ(A).toReal.
μ-a.e., |h(x)·ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c·c'·1_A(x): on A by the two bounds, off A because h vanishes off W and on K.
|T(φ)| = |∫ g dμ| ≤ ∫ c·c'·1_A dμ = c·c'·μ(W∖K) (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).

subproblems.title: Cut-off estimate for f·L^*(dy¹∧…∧dyⁿ) given the pullback bound (H1) and cut-offs (H2) with b = 1 on L(K): |T(f·θ_L)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K) (Step 7 of the parent proof; Simon 6, proof of Lemma 2.36, display (2))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, and U, W, K ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, W ⊆ U and K compact. Let T ∈ D_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), μ a measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ (for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U), x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x)), and assume μ(W∖K) ≠ ∞. Let L : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ be a continuous linear map and θ_L := wedgeCovectors n (fun i => y^i∘L) ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n, where y^i = EuclideanSpace.proj i are the coordinate functions on ℝⁿ. Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ W, and let c, c' ∈ ℝ with |f(x)| ≤ c for every x and |ξ(x)(θ_L)| ≤ c' for μ-a.e. x. Write 𝓛ⁿ for Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝⁿ. Assume (H1): there is C ∈ ℝ such that |T(φ)| ≤ C·M·(𝓛ⁿ(tsupport a))^{1/n} for every C^∞ compactly supported a : ℝⁿ → ℝ, every M ∈ ℝ with |a(y)| ≤ M for all y, and every φ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ(x) = (f(x)·a(L(x)))·θ_L for all x; here 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport a) is read as a real number (toReal) and 1/n = 1/((m : ℝ) + 1). Assume (H2): for every δ > 0 there is a C^∞ compactly supported b : ℝⁿ → ℝ with 0 ≤ b(y) ≤ 1 for all y, b(y) = 1 for all y ∈ L(K), and 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ (as a real number). Then every ζ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with ζ(x) = f(x)·θ_L for all x satisfies |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K), with μ(W∖K) read as a real number (toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U W K : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ ξ → IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → IsCompact K → μ (W \ K) ≠ ∞ → ∀ (L : Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl (m + 1)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (c c' : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ W → (∀ x, |f x| ≤ c) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |ξ x (wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp L))| ≤ c') → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ a : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) a → HasCompactSupport a → ∀ M : ℝ, (∀ y, |a y| ≤ M) → ∀ φ : TestFormOn U (m + 1), (∀ x, (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = (f x * a (L x)) • wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp L)) → |T φ| ≤ C * M * ((volume (tsupport a)).toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / ((m : ℝ) + 1))) → (∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ b : Eucl (m + 1) → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) b ∧ HasCompactSupport b ∧ (∀ y, 0 ≤ b y ∧ b y ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ y ∈ L '' K, b y = 1) ∧ ((volume : Measure (Eucl (m + 1))) (tsupport b)).toReal ≤ δ) → ∀ ζ : TestFormOn U (m + 1), (∀ x, (ζ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) x = f x • wedgeCovectors (m + 1) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.proj i : Eucl (m + 1) →L[ℝ] ℝ).comp L)) → |T ζ| ≤ c * c' * (μ (W \ K)).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 7 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of Lemma 2.36, display (2)) for one index α. The parent applies it with L := π_α, f := ω_α, c := c_α, c' := c'_α and ζ := ζ_α. In the parent, (H1) is the conclusion of pullback_top_form_bound applied to T, W, f and L (it replaces Remark 2.35), and (H2) is the conclusion of null_compact_cutoff applied to the compact 𝓛ⁿ-null set F := L(K). Those two theorems are dependencies of the parent node, not of this child: here they enter only as the hypotheses (H1) and (H2). This child's own dependencies are the child theorems scalar_test_form and remainder_bound.
Write θ := θ_L = wedgeCovectors n (fun i => y^i∘L), n = m + 1, and D := μ(W∖K).toReal ≥ 0.

1. Reduction. Fix C as in (H1). It suffices to show |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·D + ε for every ε > 0; then |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·D (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). This is the parent's "letting δ ↓ 0".
2. Choice of δ and of the cut-off. Fix ε > 0. Put A := |C| + 1 > 0 and δ := (ε/A)ⁿ > 0. By (H2), choose b : ℝⁿ → ℝ, C^∞ with compact support, with 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, b = 1 on L(K) and 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ.
3. The form φ₁. Let g(x) := f(x)·b(L(x)). The map b∘L is C^∞, being the composition of the C^∞ map b with the continuous linear map L; a product of C^∞ functions is C^∞ (ContDiff.mul, ContDiff.comp, ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff). Since g(x) = 0 whenever f(x) = 0, g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mul_right) and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ W ⊆ U (tsupport_mul_subset_left). By the child theorem scalar_test_form (a dependency of this child) there is φ₁ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ₁(x) = (f(x)·b(L(x)))·θ for every x.
4. The φ₁-term is small. Since 0 ≤ b ≤ 1, |b(y)| ≤ 1 for every y. Apply (H1) with a := b, M := 1 and φ := φ₁: |T(φ₁)| ≤ C·1·v, where v := (𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b))^{1/n} ≥ 0 (a real power of a nonnegative real). As 0 ≤ 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ and t ↦ t^{1/n} is monotone on [0, ∞) (Real.rpow_le_rpow, exponent 1/n ≥ 0), we get v ≤ δ^{1/n} = ((ε/A)ⁿ)^{1/n} = ε/A. Here 1/((m : ℝ) + 1) = ((m + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ and ε/A ≥ 0 (Real.pow_rpow_inv_natCast). Therefore |T(φ₁)| ≤ C·v ≤ |C|·v ≤ |C|·ε/A ≤ ε, since v ≥ 0 and |C| ≤ A.
5. The form φ₂. Let φ₂ := ζ − φ₁ ∈ Dⁿ(U); Dⁿ(U) is a submodule. For every x, φ₂(x) = f(x)·θ − (f(x)·b(L(x)))·θ = h(x)·θ with h(x) := f(x)·(1 − b(L(x))); evaluate both covectors at an arbitrary tuple and use ring arithmetic.
6. Properties of h.
 (i) |h(x)| = |f(x)|·|1 − b(L(x))| ≤ |f(x)| ≤ c, since 0 ≤ 1 − b(L(x)) ≤ 1.
 (ii) If x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport f because tsupport f ⊆ W. So f(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and h(x) = 0. This is the parent's "if x ∉ W, then x ∉ tsupport ω_α, so ω_α(x) = 0".
 (iii) If x ∈ K, then L(x) ∈ L(K), so b(L(x)) = 1 and h(x) = 0. This is the parent's "if x ∈ K, then π_αx ∈ F_α, so b(π_αx) = 1".
7. The φ₂-term. Apply the child theorem remainder_bound (a dependency of this child) to U, W, K, T, μ, ξ (representation, W open, K compact, μ(W∖K) ≠ ∞), to θ, h, c, c' (Step 6 and the hypothesis |ξ(x)(θ)| ≤ c' for μ-a.e. x), and to φ := φ₂ (Step 5). It gives |T(φ₂)| ≤ c·c'·D.
8. Combination. ζ = φ₁ + φ₂ in Dⁿ(U), so T(ζ) = T(φ₁) + T(φ₂) by linearity of T. By Steps 4 and 7, |T(ζ)| ≤ |T(φ₁)| + |T(φ₂)| ≤ ε + c·c'·D. By Step 1, |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·D. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix C from (H1). For ε > 0 put δ := (ε/(|C|+1))ⁿ and take a cut-off b from (H2) (b = 1 on L(K), 𝓛ⁿ(tsupport b) ≤ δ).
scalar_test_form gives φ₁ ∈ Dⁿ(U) with φ₁ = (f·(b∘L))·θ_L. (H1) with a = b and M = 1 gives |T(φ₁)| ≤ |C|·δ^{1/n} ≤ ε.
φ₂ := ζ − φ₁ = (f·(1 − b∘L))·θ_L. Its coefficient is bounded by c and vanishes off W and on K.
remainder_bound gives |T(φ₂)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K). Adding gives |T(ζ)| ≤ c·c'·μ(W∖K) + ε; let ε ↓ 0.
